title: Raleigh police use Marinus Analytics' Traffic Jam to link phone numbers and photos across cities in a live trafficking case
summary: CBN (18 Oct 2017) shows Raleigh PD detectives using Traffic Jam, a CMU-born tool with facial recognition over escort ads, to corroborate a trafficker's movements; outcomes stated only as aggregates.
account: The date is CBN's publication; the case described was ongoing. Major Richard Hoffman of the Raleigh Police Department told CBN that Traffic Jam lets investigators link a potential victim to another victim and then to a suspect, and that its image search returns historical images tied to the same phone number or similar image. Detective Rob Pereira described pulling a phone number from a Colorado police report into Traffic Jam to see where and when it had been used, corroborating accounts from several victims about where the trafficker was taking them. Marinus co-founder Cara Jones described the tool as applying artificial intelligence to publicly available ad data. CBN states that Traffic Jam has helped recover hundreds of victims; Futurism (2018) repeats a similar claim from CEO Emily Kennedy with an 88 percent success rate. No individually attributable rescue is documented.
purpose: Mine online sex advertisements (text, phone numbers, facial recognition on images) to help law enforcement find trafficking victims and link cases.
developer: Marinus Analytics (origin: Carnegie Mellon University undergraduate project)
taxonomy_note: Named police officials describe use on a live case, but the outcome of that case is not reported; the 'hundreds recovered' figures are vendor aggregates, so all depths are null.
